articles.title: H1 Rebound Faces Major Resistance
articles.description: Fundamental Analysis Gold has recovered strongly from the 3,980–4,000 area, but the rebound is now meeting a much more difficult macro environment. Oil prices have risen again on renewed supply concerns, increasing inflation pressure ahead of the Fed decision. Markets broadly expect the Fed to hold rates steady, while expectations for a December hike remain elevated at around 84%. The U.S. dollar is holding near a two-week high and the 10-year Treasury yield has moved back above 5%. Both factors can limit Gold’s upside because higher yields increase the opportunity cost of holding a non-yielding asset. The next major catalyst is the FOMC decision and press conference, followed by Thursday’s PCE inflation data. Technical Analysis The H1 structure remains bearish on the larger timeframe, but the short-term structure has clearly improved. Gold defended the 3,980–4,000 Support Zone, then produced a short-term CHoCH followed by BOS. This initiated the recovery shown on the chart. Price has now reached around 4,055, directly beneath the descending trendline and the marked Major Resistance Zone around 4,055–4,075. This is the first serious test of the rebound. If buyers can hold the short-term structure and break through this resistance, the next upside objective is the 4,090–4,105 Key Resistance / Upside Target. Above that, the larger 4,130–4,145 Supply Zone remains the major H1 barrier. Key Levels 4,130–4,145: Major Supply Zone 4,090–4,105: Key Resistance / Upside Target 4,055–4,075: Major Resistance + Descending Trendline 4,015–4,030: Short-term Structural Support 3,980–4,000: Major Support Zone Main Trading Scenario The primary scenario is a bullish continuation after a controlled pullback. If Gold is rejected around 4,055–4,075, a pullback toward the 4,015–4,030 Short-term Structural Support would be reasonable within the current H1 recovery structure. If buyers defend that support and regain momentum, the next target becomes 4,090–4,105. A sustained H1 acceptance above this area could open the way toward the larger 4,130–4,145 Supply Zone. The key point is that Gold does not necessarily need to break resistance immediately. Holding the newly formed higher-low structure would be more important for continuation. Risk / Invalidation The short-term bullish scenario weakens if Gold loses 4,015–4,030 with sustained H1 acceptance below the ascending structure. A deeper break through 3,980–4,000 would invalidate the current recovery structure and indicate that the recent rebound was only a corrective move inside the larger bearish trend. On the upside, failure to reclaim 4,055–4,075 keeps the descending trendline firmly in control. Marco’s View Gold has completed the first part of the recovery plan: 3,980–4,000 held, price recovered, and the market reached the first major resistance area. Now the structure becomes more interesting. The 4,055–4,075 zone is where the short-term bullish recovery meets the larger bearish trendline. A clean breakout would strengthen the path toward 4,090–4,105, while a rejection could send price back toward 4,015–4,030 for another structural test. With the FOMC decision approaching, volatility can increase sharply around these levels. The macro backdrop still favors caution because the dollar and Treasury yields remain elevated. For me, 4,055–4,075 is the key battlefield: reclaim it and the recovery can expand; reject it and the next test is 4,015–4,030.

articles.title: Ravindra Jadeja Dethroned! South Africa Star Ends India All-Rounder’s Four-Year ICC Rankings Reign
articles.description: Ravindra Jadeja has lost his long-standing grip on the top spot in the ICC Test all-rounder rankings, with South Africa’s Marco Jansen emerging as the new No. 1 in the latest update released on Wednesday, October 28. Jadeja, who had dominated the list for around four years, has slipped to second place, while Jansen’s impressive performances against Australia have propelled him to a career-best rating. There was more movement in the rankings, with India’s Abhishek Sharma climbing to the summit of the T20I batting charts. Jansen Ends Jadeja’s Test Rankings Dominance Jansen’s rise to the top of the Test all-rounder rankings follows a commanding display in the Gqeberha Test against Australia. The South African contributed 85 runs with the bat and claimed six wickets, earning him a rating of 451 points, the highest of his career. Jadeja now occupies second place with 422 points, bringing his extended spell at the summit to an end. Also Check || WATCH: South Africa Fan Trolls Nathan Lyon With Sandpaper Bangladesh’s Mehidy Hasan Miraz retains third position, while South Africa’s Wayne Mulder sits fourth. Australia’s Mitchell Starc rounds out the top five. India have another representative in the top 10, with Washington Sundar placed seventh on 234 points. South Africa’s Simon Harmer has also made significant progress, surging 15 places to eighth with 228 points. Jansen Also Claims No. 1 Spot In Test Bowling Rankings Jansen’s rise has not been limited to the all-rounder charts. The South African quick has also climbed five places to become the world’s top-ranked Test bowler, underlining his growing influence across formats of the game. His ascent has pushed Mitchell Starc down to second place in the bowling rankings, marking another major shift at the top of the ICC standings. Abhishek Sharma Takes Over T20I Batting Summit India also have reason to celebrate in the T20I rankings, where Abhishek Sharma has moved to No. 1 among batters. His record-breaking 113-run innings against New Zealand in the third T20I proved decisive in his climb to the top. Kishan, who previously held the leading position, has fallen to third, making way for his Indian teammate to claim the rankings crown.
